rootCauseHypothesis:
A persistent selection/transform gizmo appears to remain active on page load or after prior actions, and it is intercepting pointer events at the canvas center. Because the automation framework resolves clicks to the element center, every click lands on the gizmo instead of the drawing surface, so pixels cannot be placed away from the center. This suggests a hosting-side UI state issue: stale selection state, an overlay with higher z-index/pointer-events, or a canvas coordinate mapping problem that makes automated clicks collapse to the center. Underlying error: TEST BLOCKED

The test could not be run — the UI state and the automated click constraints prevent placing pixels at coordinates away from the canvas center, which is required by the test steps.

Observations:
- Automated clicks resolve to the center of the canvas element; a persistent selection/transform gizmo (Sel: 1x1) occupies the canvas center and intercepts clicks, preventing placement of pixels in other quadrants.
- Multiple remediation attempts were made (pressing Escape, closing the tool preview, selecting the Base Layer, re-selecting Pen) but the transform gizmo remained and continued to intercept clicks.
- Because the core actions (drawing upper-left and lower-right strokes and selecting only the upper-left stroke) cannot be performed under these constraints, the required browser-verifiable behavior cannot be exercised in this run.

recommendedFixTarget.rationale: Make the canvas interaction deterministic and test-friendly: ensure the default tool state is a plain drawing mode with no persistent selection/transform overlay active on load, and clear any existing selection gizmo before automated input begins. If the app supports selection handles, either disable hit-testing on the center gizmo when not actively resizing/moving, or provide a dedicated way to dismiss it (e.g. clicking empty canvas, pressing Escape, or a reset action) that reliably removes the overlay. Also verify that canvas click coordinates are mapped correctly to the intended drawing area in the browser automation environment (including CSS scaling/devicePixelRatio), so clicks can reach all quadrants instead of always resolving to the center. If needed, add a known initial state for tests such as loading a fresh document/new layer with no active selection and no modal/tool preview blocking the canvas.
